newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia may close oil palm sector to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia may close oil palm sector to foreigners.

text.p: Indonesia may close the oil palm sector to foreign investors if a study being undertaken shows their participation in the industry had reached maximum levels, the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Friday.

Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo was quoted as saying he did not discount the possibility of placing the sector under the Negative Investment List (NGI) if a government study showed foreign involvement in the sector had hit maximum.
"To be included or not in the DNI (NGI) would depend on the outcome of the review," he was quoted as telling reporters.
"If the evaluation says opportunities for foreigners should be closed, the sector will be included in the DNI," he said.

The Investment Coordinating Board's head of Licencing, Andung Nitimihardja, was quoted as saying a temporary suspension of approving investments in the sector pending the review would affect six foreign applications, four of them from Malaysia.
Minister Sastrowardoyo said the freeze on foreign applications to set up oil palm plantations was aimed at increasing local participation.
He said Indonesia currently had prepared 5.5 million hectares for oil palm cultivation, of which approval had been given out for two million hectares.
Industry sources said any move by Indonesia to halt foreign investment in the oil palm sector would hurt Malaysia, which is faced with a shortage of labour and cultivable land.
